137114.overview: You play as Boris the Miner and must fill your rail truck with diamonds. Each screen contains three diamonds which must be collected and placed in the moving truck before it reaches the right of the screen in order to progress to the next screen. Failure to do so results in the loss of a life. The moving platform can aid you, but you must contend with the evil Orbis and it's friends.

155885.overview: Simulated pinball machine in full color graphics.

162523.overview: Enter the deadly catacombs and destroy the phantoms. One touch by a phantom is fatal so use your laser pistol. Full screen. Three dimensional graphics. Every maze is different. Includes training mode.

175428.overview:
Just as the name implies, Pengon is a clone of Sega/Coreland's old arcade game, Pengo. You play Willy the penguin, who is trapped in a maze filled with dangerous mutant sea lions. Willy's only defense is to push the blocks of ice that the screen is made up of, so that the blocks hit the sea lions and crush them against the walls.

Of note is the difference between the versions; the original program was made in America for the Tandy Colour, then ported to Dragon 32 and published by Microdeal, who liked the name enough to put it on Pengo clones for the Commodore and Atari which graphically have little in common with the CoCo game.

175432.overview:
Planet Invasion is a straight-forward Defender clone. As in the original, you patrol a horizontally scrolling landscape infested with Praetorian invaders which you must shoot down with your ship. The aliens are out to grab the Caloxin crystals scattered on the surface. If a Grabber alien gets away with it, it turns into a nastier Killer. A third kind is the Chaser, which flies quickly after you if you wait for too long. Others are the Miners, which drop mines, and Beamers, which split into three Berserkers.

For a game for the Tandy Coco and Dragon 32, Planet Invasion scrolls very quickly, though the speed comes at a cost – the landscape itself is only made up of a dotted line. Apart from that, Invasion is fairly feature-complete, having both a radar overview of the level, hyperspace and a smart bomb.

175513.overview:
Pedro's flower gardens are famed throughout Mexico - unfortunately for him, information as to their quality appears to have reached the animal kingdom. His prized flowers are under attack from hordes of animals, which must be stopped.

Pedro's task is to set up blockades and barriers to cut off the animals' routes to his flowers. He will have to take multiple trips to block off any particular path. Smaller animals can also be stopped by stamping on them.

When flowers are eaten, Pedro must replenish them by planting seeds - allowing time for them to grow, as the game is lost if all the seeds are gone. As well as the animals, he must watch out for the Tramp, who tries to steal his seeds.

The game is viewed in a 3D forced perspective, although movement is purely 2D.

175573.overview: You are a normal person, finding oneself in the strange world of Piland, a surreal place containing the secret of the wondrous Golden Sundial of Pi. After figuring out how to properly enter Piland, you must find clues to the Sundial's location, with the help (and hindrance) of the Piman, a strange little creature with distinct likes and dislikes. The Sundial is not actually in the game - it was the prize of a contest, won using the clues within the game.

175783.overview: A Pac-Man game with a sci-fi twist, Pac Droids has you piloting a space ship in a maze patrolled by flying saucers. As in the real Pac-Man, you gobble up dots while avoiding the saucers, clearing the level by eating all dots. Also, you have power-pills which turn your ship into a cross hair. Pressing fire will fire in the direction you're moving, eliminating all ghosts and dots which get in your way. You have three shots per life. Even in your cross hairs mode, the blue saucer must be avoided, since it is invincible to your shots. Enemies will also lay mines, which are easily confused with power pills.

446517.overview:
Picture Puzzles is a 1-player sliding block puzzle for the Dragon 32/64.

Each puzzle is 4 x 4 blocks. There are a total of 6 puzzle pictures spread over 2 tapes, and players can input their own pictures.

446519.overview: This is adventure #2 in Scott Adam's text adventure series. In this adventure, you shuffle between three locales: an unremarkable (at first) London flat and two islands littered with dangerous critters and people. The goal of the game is to find the two pirate treasures on the treasure island. You move about and use objects by typing one or two word commands such as NORTH, INVENTORY, or GET SNEAKERS. You only have to type the first 3 letters of a command or object for the parser to recognize it.

446528.overview:
Photo Finish is a 1–4 player horse race gambling game for the Dragon 32/64.

Each player starts with $100, and can bet on the winner or ends of six horse races. The player then watches the horses race and sees a photo finish at the end. The race results and payout are shown after each race. Players are eliminated when they run out of money.

446530.overview: The player is aboard the luxury liner S. S. Poseidon. A huge undersea earthquake has caused a tidal wave which has capsized the ship. It is floating bottom-up on the surface and taking on water. Your goal is simply to get out alive. The player has a limited number of turns to escape the sinking ship before it goes down based upon difficulty level.

446554.overview: The player is walking through the peaceful Oxfordshire countryside, when they smell burning. In The Burning Farmhouse, the player controls a blue cross within a burning building. The player must avoid deadly flames represented by red circles. The player can examine, open, and take items, and must escape with Pettigrew's Diary. This sends the player on a grand adventure through Europe in search of great treasure.

456100.overview: An Egyptian Treasure Hunt leads you into the dark recesses of a recently uncovered Pyramid. Will you recover all the treasures or more likely will you join its denizens for that long eternal sleep?
